examples.text: Я потом всё объясню.
examples.trans: I'll explain everything later.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Сеня, иди быстро работай на кухню!
examples.trans: Senya, go work in the kitchen right now!

examples.text: Зачем мне вообще туда идти?
examples.trans: Why would I even go there at all?

examples.text: Лёва, иди сюда на одну минуту.
examples.trans: Lyova, come here for one minute.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to work', forming an aspectual pair with 'поработать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Давайте активно работать, господа.
examples.trans: Let's work actively, gentlemen.

examples.text: Нормальные повара спокойно работают на кухне.
examples.trans: Normal cooks work quietly in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Будем трудиться на общее благо.
